pages.text: Red apples ripened on the tree beside the cabin. So many, the branches bent.
Nils wanted a basketful. The storeroom beside the cabin kept food. They would take apples from it all winter.
Nils picked one apple. The basket was still empty. "When will I finish?"
He held the trunk and shook. Tumble, tumble! Apples fell like rain.
"Wow! Finished already!" Apples lay all over the ground. Nils happily gathered them.
Grandpa gently pressed one. The pressed spot was dark and soft. Nils looked at it.
Every gathered apple was bruised. "Bruised apples rot quickly in the storeroom." The basket emptied again.
Grandpa reached out and gently twisted off an apple. "Gently hand-picked apples keep well until winter."
Nils gently picked one at a time from low branches. Grandpa took the high ones. The basket steadily filled.
Full! They put apples in rows on the storeroom shelves. Bruised ones went separately, for the winter birds.
